title: Articulated 3D Scene Graphs for Open-World Mobile Manipulation
abstract: arXiv:2602.16356v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Semantic scene understanding has enabled robots to reason and perform affordance-driven object interaction. Despite this, real-world manipulation remains fundamentally limited by the inability to predict how objects move and are articulated. Long-horizon mobile manipulation requires closing the gap between semantics, geometry, and kinematics. In this work, we present MoMa-SG, a novel framework for building semantic-kinematic 3D scene graphs of articulated scenes containing a myriad of interactable objects. Given RGB-D sequences containing multiple object articulations, we temporally segment object interactions and infer object motion using occlusion-robust point tracking. We lift point trajectories to 3D and estimate articulation models using a novel unified twist estimation formulation that robustly estimates revolute and prismatic joint parameters in a single optimization pass. translated_title: 面向开放世界移动操作的铰接式3D场景图
translated_abstract: 语义场景理解已经使机器人能够进行推理并执行基于可供性的物体交互。尽管如此，现实世界的操作仍然从根本上受限于无法预测物体如何运动以及如何被铰接。长时程移动操作需要弥合语义、几何与运动学之间的差距。在这项工作中，我们提出了MoMa-SG，一个用于为包含大量可交互物体的铰接场景构建语义-运动学3D场景图的新颖框架。给定包含多个物体铰接运动的RGB-D序列，我们对物体交互进行时间上的分割，并使用遮挡鲁棒的点跟踪来推断物体运动。我们将点轨迹提升到3D空间，并使用一种新颖的统一扭转估计公式来估计铰接模型，该公式能够在单次优化过程中稳健地估计旋转关节和移动关节的参数。接下来，我们将物体与铰接关系进行关联……
tldr: 提出了MoMa-SG框架，通过遮挡鲁棒的点跟踪和单次优化即可估计旋转与移动关节参数的统一扭转估计方法，从RGB-D序列构建语义-运动学3D场景图，以弥合语义、几何与运动学之间的差距，支持开放世界长时程移动操作。
en_tdlr: MoMa-SG is a novel framework that builds semantic-kinematic 3D scene graphs from RGB-D sequences using occlusion-robust point tracking and a unified twist estimation formulation that robustly estimates revolute and prismatic joint parameters in a single optimization pass, bridging semantics, geometry, and kinematics for open-world long-horizon mobile manipulation.
